meta.description: Benchmark sources behind the Tech Value pages, collected or planned, with the metric each reports and the configuration details recorded for every result.

sources.name: SPEC CPU 2017 published results
sources.licence: SPEC Fair Use Rules (https://www.spec.org/products/fairuse). Public use is allowed when the source and retrieval date are stated, the licensee of each result is identifiable, the SPEC trademarks are acknowledged, SPEC metrics are compared only with SPEC metrics of the same benchmark release, and derived values and estimates are clearly labelled and never called SPEC metrics. The site does all of these.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; SPEC publishes new results about every two weeks
sources.typical_lag: results appear weeks to months after the test date

sources.name: SPEC Graphics and Workstation Performance Group (GWPG) published results
sources.licence: SPEC Fair Use Rules (https://www.spec.org/products/fairuse). Public use is allowed when the source and retrieval date are stated, the licensee of each result is identifiable, the SPEC, SPECviewperf, SPECworkstation and SPECapc trademarks are acknowledged, SPEC metrics are compared only within the same benchmark release and resolution, and derived values and estimates are clearly labelled and never called SPEC metrics. The site does all of these.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; SPEC/GWPG publishes new workstation and GPU results periodically
sources.typical_lag: results appear weeks to months after the test date

sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots
sources.licence: CC0 (Creative Commons Zero), stated on https://opendata.blender.org/download/ and in the LICENSE.txt shipped in each snapshot. No conditions on reuse; the site credits it anyway.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; snapshots are regenerated daily

data.publisher: Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation (vendor submissions, reviewed by SPEC)
data.metric: SPECrate2017_int_base and _peak; this site uses base per socket
data.recorded: OEM, system, chips, cores, threads per core, clock, cache, memory, compiler, OS, test and publication dates, disclosure link

data.publisher: SPEC Graphics and Workstation Performance Group (OEM and vendor submissions)
data.benchmark: SPECviewperf 12.1/13/2020/15 (Windows and Linux), SPECworkstation 3.0/3.1/4.0, SPECapc (Solidworks 2022/2024/2025, Siemens NX 2024, Maya 2024, Creo 9, 3ds Max 2020)
data.metric: Each suite's GPU measurement (viewset geometric mean, SPECapc GPU composite or viewport workloads, SPECworkstation graphics subsystem); compared raw within suite, version, OS and resolution, combined only where the calibration passes its check
data.recorded: OEM, system, CPU, GPU as written, OS, resolution, anti-aliasing, test date, metric, number of viewsets, composite, best and worst viewset, disclosure link
data.used_for: Over & under performers (GPU), results by workload

data.publisher: SPEC Graphics and Workstation Performance Group (OEM submissions)
data.metric: The CPU subsystem score of one SPECworkstation version; never mixed with SPEC CPU 2017 and not used by the CPU models
data.recorded: Submitter, system, CPU and GPU as written, suite version, disclosure link
data.used_for: Catalogue measurements for desktop and workstation CPUs SPEC CPU 2017 does not cover

data.metric: Median samples per minute over runs, per device and Blender version
data.recorded: Device, CPU or GPU, Blender version, number of runs, median and interquartile range
data.used_for: Value ranking, Fair price, comparisons, and its own over & under performer models (CPU and GPU), kept apart from the SPEC ones

data.source: SPEC CPU 2017 floating point and speed
data.metric: Would be a separate workload view, never combined with Integer
Each test's own unit; compared only within one test, version and setting
data.status: Blocked: every page answers automated clients with a Cloudflare challenge (checked 2026-11-20 from a home PC)
data.used_for: Not collected: would add consumer CPUs and GPUs SPEC does not cover, if the operator allows automated access

data.benchmark: Geekbench 5 and 6 CPU and GPU compute
data.status: Not used: the Geekbench licence gives Primate Labs exclusive rights to uploaded results, and robots.txt disallows its search pages (checked 2026-11-20)

data.benchmark: PerformanceTest CPU Mark and G3D Mark
data.status: Not used: PassMark says its data may not be copied without a licence (checked 2026-11-20)

data.benchmark: Relative performance (TechPowerUp's own summary of its reviews)
data.status: Not used: no export or reuse terms, and its robots.txt could not be read by this project's fetcher (checked 2026-11-20)
Not used: scattered across copyrighted reviews with no structured source to collect automatically

data.publisher: Reviewers and papers (not reviewed by SPEC)
data.benchmark: SPEC CPU 2017 and SPECviewperf run outside SPEC's process
data.metric: Would be labelled as unofficial and kept apart from SPEC-published results
